mine: No one born of a forbidden union
note: Hebrew mamzer (only here and Zech 9:6) is of uncertain meaning; Jewish tradition takes it as the offspring of incest or adultery, not simply a child born out of wedlock as "bastard" implies. (Hebrew 23:3 = KJV 23:2.)

mine: a digging tool among your equipment
note: Hebrew 'azen is a hapax usually taken as "equipment, gear" (related to zayin "weapon" only by guess); yated is a peg or digging stick. (Hebrew 23:14 = KJV 23:13.)

kjv: no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite
mine: None of the daughters of Israel shall be a cult prostitute ... a cult prostitute
note: Hebrew qedeshah and qadesh ("consecrated one") denote persons attached to a shrine for sexual rites; the KJV's "whore" and "sodomite" lose the cultic sense, and v. 19 then uses the ordinary word zonah for a prostitute. (Hebrew 23:18 = KJV 23:17.)
Hebrew neshekh means any interest on a loan; "usury" in modern English means excessive interest, which wrongly narrows the prohibition. (Hebrew 23:20-21 = KJV 23:19-20.)
